body:
A run hit this: `grep` cuts long lines to ~200 characters around the match (`lockdown.rs::around`), marking the cut with a leading `…`. An agent copied the visible tail of a 2,140-character fixture line into a patch hunk; the hunk couldn't match (a patch line is a whole line, D-142), the patch was refused (E0108), and the agent recovered with one `write --replace` call. The bare `…` was easy to miss.

The E0108 refusal already names the fix; the gap is at read time, before the patch is written.

Fix: when a grep reply shows any line whose start was cut (the `…` prefix from `around`), add one footer line, in the style of the existing "N more files match" footers:

`Lines starting with … are cut from longer lines; read the whole line with read <path> --lines <n>..<n>, and to change part of one use write <path> --replace with old/text.`

- One footer per reply, not per line; only when at least one shown line was cut at the start.
- Context lines (`12-`) cut the same way count.
- `read` needs no change: it shows whole lines within its budget.

Checks: unit tests in `lockdown.rs` — a reply with a cut match line gets the footer; a reply with only whole lines doesn't; the footer appears once per reply.
title: grep: cut lines say so and name the fix
